Hi Sarah — looping in with technical responses to the KMS/encryption questions. High level: 

- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering our hosted control plane and inference runtime. We generally share the full report under NDA; the redwood_soc2_summary_2025.pdf Marissa attached covers the high-level scope.

- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA workloads in Dedicated and Private deployment models. We can execute a BAA for customers who need it. Hosted customers can be supported depending on contractual terms and data flow — we'll scope that in the security deep-dive.

- In-transit & At-rest encryption: TLS 1.2+ (recommended TLS 1.3) for all external traffic. At-rest encryption uses AES-256 for model artifacts and cache; sensitive metadata can be isolated in Private/Dedicated setups.

- Customer-managed keys (CMK): we support BYOK patterns. For AWS: Redwood can be configured to use customer CMKs via AWS KMS to encrypt storage volumes and key-wrap secrets — keys are not exported to Redwood; operations may use KMS API calls with customer IAM roles. For HSM-backed requirements we offer integrations via partner HSMs in Private deployments (HSMs or CloudHSM).

- Key storage: Redwood does not persist customer private key material. We rely on customer KMS/HSM for key operations (encrypt/decrypt/wrap) and we can configure strict KMS key policies and audit logs.

I've attached a short KMS integration guide with the technical flow and recommended IAM roles. Happy to walk through this on Wed Mar 4 during the proposed deep-dive.

Attachment: kms_integration_guide.pdf

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
